propositions: Raw event files must be read (not compiled state) for metrics requiring per-event or multi-occurrence data: attempts_per_ticket (distinct claim sessions), rework_within_days (closed→open→closed edges), and reopen_recovery (all reopened edges).
Compiled state from reduce_ticket suffices for terminal-value metrics: first_pass_rate (last_reopened_at absence), revert_recovery (reverts[] with target_event_type filter for STATUS/COMMITS only).

Event reader helpers must reuse existing reducer utilities: event_sort_key for chronological ordering, is_active_event for compaction-retired inclusion, and resolve_ticket_dir_name for directory resolution — no reinvention of file-listing or sorting.
Metrics return None (→ Unavailable) for empty date ranges; a range with no qualifying tickets but with events returns measured zero (0), not None.

Unit tests must cover: two-session attempts (==2), closed→open→closed 3 days apart in rework_within_days(7) but not 10 days apart, first_pass_rate for never-reopened tickets, revert_recovery filtering on target_event_type (STATUS/COMMITS counted, COMMENT-reverts excluded), and retired events included in counts.
